panels.title: Session Timers
panels.description:
Session lifetime timers, ONE stat panel with three tiles SIDE-BY-SIDE (orientation=vertical => columns). LAST ACK = seconds since the main loop last acked ANY claude-event (time() - claude_mainloop_last_ack_timestamp_seconds; green<360, amber>=360, red>=600). That is the whole liveness story: the loop runs `event-ack ack-batch` after every event batch it handles, which stamps last-ack-timestamp, and `claude-watch metrics` exports it. A wedged loop stops acking and this climbs. CLAUDE UPTIME = seconds since the Claude Code process started (claude_process_start_timestamp_seconds, derived from /proc so it renders on a bare host AND in a container). SINCE CLEAR = seconds since the context was last RESET -- a /clear (daemon auto-clear, self-clear, or hand-typed) or a compaction, all of which throw the context away and rebuild it (n/a if none recorded). The daemon stamps it on the check cycle where it OBSERVES the reset, so the value trails the actual reset by at most one check_interval; it recognises a reset from a below-30K token sample OR a halved token counter, the latter because a fresh context on a big-preamble session boots well above 30K and would otherwise never be seen (2026-08-22: a 907979 -> 77185 clear went unrecorded and this tile read 1.07 days 50 minutes after the clear). There used to be a fourth tile, LAST ACK AGE, fed by the age of a marker claude-event-watch wrote each time it surfaced a heartbeat-tick. It and the HEARTBEAT tile (the heartbeat FILE's mtime) were two approximations of the same question, and the marker lived inside the event queue dir where a health-check counted it as an unconsumed event and fired false WATCHER DOWN alerts. Both are retired (2026-08-22); this single tile measures the quantity directly. No value => the loop has never acked, rendered as "n/a" (kept short: the old tile's explanatory n/a string overflowed at every width).

VALUE SIZE IS BOUNDED BY THE PHONE, not by the desktop: at 390px the panel stacks to full width and each tile gets about 93px of text, so a value like `57.7 mins` wraps its unit onto a second line and grows DOWNWARD -- at 32px that pushed the wrapped unit past the bottom of the h=4 panel and clipped the two-line "Claude Uptime" name against the header, while 24px clears both by a full line. Check any change to options.text.valueSize at phone width, not at 1520px.

panels.title: Tokens / Minute (excl. cache reads)
panels.description:
Tokens per minute, averaged over 1m / 5m / 15m. claude_code_tokens_total is a cumulative COUNTER, so each tile is rate(...[window]) * 60 — never the raw counter. type="cache_read" is excluded: cache reads re-count the whole cached prefix on every request and dominate the sum by ~300x, which would make the tiles read in the millions rather than the actual burn rate.

VALUE SIZE: these values are short single tokens (`0`, `9 K`) and stay clear at 390px even at 32px, but options.text.valueSize is 24 to match Session Timers, which shares this band and cannot go above 24 on a phone -- two panels of the same shape at different value sizes read as a difference in importance.

panels.title: Build Info
panels.description:
Identity of the RUNNING daemon binary, as three tiles: version, the commit it was built from, and the PR that commit came in on. All three come from ONE source -- the claude_watch_build_info gauge the daemon's textfile collector writes (src/metrics.rs), stamped at build time from git (build.rs) -- so this panel makes NO network call and needs NO GitHub token/PAT, ever. They only move on a deploy.

SINGLE-DATASOURCE ON PURPOSE (2026-08-25, Andrew #5548, recurring #5482). This panel used to be `-- Mixed --`: it batched a third, GitHub-sourced tile ("latest merged", now its own "Latest Merged PR" panel to the right) into the same query. Grafana's /api/ds/query sends every target of a Mixed panel in ONE request and fails the WHOLE response the instant ANY one target errors -- and the GitHub target was unauthenticated (60 req/hr/IP) and/or dependent on the Infinity plugin/datasource being provisioned, either of which fails routinely. That is exactly why this panel would go warning-icon-blank except for a stale commit value: the GitHub tile's failure took the two healthy Prometheus tiles down with it. Splitting the GitHub tile into its own panel, on its own datasource, means this panel now has exactly one target on one datasource (Prometheus) -- nothing outside Prometheus itself can blank it again.

TILE PLUMBING. The gauge's VALUE is a constant 1 and everything interesting is in its labels, so a labelsToFields transformation promotes version/commit/pr to fields; filterFieldsByName drops the scrape-added labels (instance/job/source) that would otherwise show up as extra tiles; pr is converted to a number so the `prefix:#` unit renders #714 instead of "714"; organize renames pr -> PR to match the tile-name casing.

GEOMETRY IS LOAD-BEARING. A stat tile only stacks its name above its value while the tile is at most ~2.5x wider than it is tall; past that ratio Grafana switches to the wide layout and puts the name to the LEFT of the value. Three tiles in a full-width 24-column panel would need h=9 to stack -- half width (w=12) with h=5 puts each tile at roughly 310x155 and stacks, the same shape as the Session Timers tiles at the top of the board. That is why this panel is half width and its band is one of the few here whose widths do not sum to 24 -- the left half is the "Latest Merged PR" panel. Widening or shortening flips the tiles back onto one line, so move w and h together.

VALUE SIZE IS BOUNDED BY THE PHONE, not the desktop: options.text.valueSize is 24, chosen at 390px width where 26px grazes and 28px collides with the neighbouring tile. Check any change to it at phone width, not desktop.

panels.title: Latest Merged PR
panels.description:
The repo's side of "what shipped last": the most recently MERGED pull request on GitHub. Complements Build Info to its right -- a gap between the PR shown here and the PR the RUNNING binary was built from (Build Info's "PR" tile) is un-deployed work.

Read directly from GitHub by the Infinity datasource (uid `infinity`, backend parser), NOT from Prometheus -- there is deliberately no exporter behind it, since a local exporter scraping GitHub for one already-public number is one more service to run, restart and forget. UNAUTHENTICATED: GitHub allows 60 requests/hour/IP without a token, and one dashboard refresh with this panel in the viewport is one request, so this dashboard's 5m refresh caps the worst case at 12/hour. A deployment that wants sub-minute refresh back should give the Infinity datasource a GitHub token (5,000/hour) first (monitoring/dashboards/README.md). Where the Infinity datasource is not provisioned this panel simply flags a missing datasource; nothing else on the board is affected.

STANDALONE SINCE 2026-08-25 (Andrew #5548, recurring #5482): this tile used to share a `-- Mixed --` datasource panel with Build Info's two Prometheus tiles. Grafana batches every target of a Mixed panel into one /api/ds/query request and fails the WHOLE response the moment any one target errors -- so a GitHub rate-limit or a missing Infinity datasource blanked Build Info's otherwise-healthy version/commit/PR tiles too, not just this one. Moving this tile onto its own panel, on its own single datasource, confines a GitHub outage to this one tile from now on.

RANKING IS BY merged_at, NOT BY PR NUMBER. The JSONata root selector `$[merged_at != null]^(>merged_at)[0]` drops closed-but-never-merged PRs, sorts what is left by merge time descending and takes the first. Number order inverts merged order routinely -- two PRs open at once merge in whichever order goes green first -- so `max(number)` would show the wrong PR every time that happens. The URL's sort=updated is only a cheap way to get recent PRs into the first page; a comment or a label bumps updated_at without merging anything, so the ordering that matters is redone here.

panels.title: Output Tokens (by model, period)
panels.description: Cumulative OUTPUT tokens by model over the dashboard's time range (increase() of the windowed claude_output_tokens_total gauge; Andrew #5370 — tokens = cumulative OUTPUT, split by model).

panels.title: Ack Staleness
panels.description: Seconds since the main loop last acked ANY claude-event, over time. The stat tile above shows the current value; this shows whether it is a spike or a trend. Renamed from "Heartbeat Staleness" 2026-08-22 when the host heartbeat file was retired in favour of the ack timestamp.

panels.title: Reminder Fires by Type (rate / 5m)
panels.description: Rate of hook-driven reminder fires. context_high fires when context % crosses the high threshold; version_update fires when a new claude version is detected; pre_compact fires before a compaction.

panels.title: Fallback Injections by Type (rate / 5m)
panels.description: Rate of daemon-driven fallback injections. When nonzero, Claude ignored the corresponding reminder and the daemon had to intervene (force /clear or /restart).

panels.title: Cooperation Ratio (30m)
panels.description: Fraction of context_high reminders that Claude acted on autonomously (did NOT require fallback). Computed as 1 - (fallback clear rate / context_high reminder rate) over 30m. Target >= 0.8. Falls back to 1.0 when no reminders fired in the window.

panels.title: Reminder→Action Latency (avg)
panels.description: Average time from reminder fire to Claude action (self-/clear or /restart), split by type. Computed as sum/count since the exporter ships counter pairs rather than a true histogram -- this is an AVERAGE, not a real quantile. Samples only when Claude acted within 1h (context) / 6h (version).

panels.title: Counter Values (debug)
panels.description: Raw counter values for debugging: reminder_fires and fallback_injections by type, plus latency sum/count pairs.

panels.title: Total Interrupts (24h)
panels.description: Sum of all claude_interrupts_total increases across every kind over the last 24h. Red above 50 (wedge-state territory), yellow above 20.

panels.title: Interrupts per Kind (1h)
panels.description: Per-kind count of interrupts fired in the last hour. Quick triage to spot which kind is currently firing.

panels.title: Interrupts by Kind (rate / min)
panels.description: Per-minute rate of claude_interrupts_total by kind, smoothed over 5m. Stacked area. Key chart for noise monitoring and cascade detection.

panels.title: Cascade Indicator (10m avg /min)
panels.description: Total interrupts per minute averaged over 10m. Red > 2/min indicates cascade state (like yesterday's wedge).

panels.title: Tokens This Month (MTD)
panels.description: Total Claude Code token usage for the current calendar month. Sums input + output + cache_creation + cache_read across all retained transcripts whose timestamp falls in this month. Resets on the 1st.

panels.title: Token Usage by Day
panels.description: Rolling 24h token usage stacked by type. With only partial-day data the bars show today's running total; once multi-day data accumulates the chart shows the rolling 24h window as a time series. Bars are stacked input/output/cache_creation/cache_read.

panels.title: Tool Calls (by tool)
panels.description: Fleet-wide tool calls, by tool name (claude_tool_use_total) — a windowed gauge folded over every live/recent transcript, not a monotonic counter.

panels.title: Agents Spawned
panels.description: Distinct Claude Code subagent transcripts observed in the live/recent window (claude_agent_spawned_count) — a windowed gauge, not a lifetime total.
